subject: Renewal: proposal to rebalance bundle and convert vouchers to top-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@scalegrid.ai>, Procurement <procurement@scalegrid.ai>
Cc: Drew Matthews <drew@scalegrid.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: proposal to rebalance bundle and convert vouchers to top-up

Hi Ava / procurement team —

Thanks for the heads-up about the upcoming renewal window. Quick background: ScaleGrid is coming up on their 12‑month renewal (Dec 12), and they sit on a mix of 200K voucher credits from our Q1 pilot plus a growing consumption profile (embedding-heavy, bursty inference). They asked if we can both:

- Convert the remaining vouchers to a top-up SKU (so it shows up as committed units on invoice)
- Rebalance their bundle from a seat-forward model into a proportional capacity/top-up structure for the next 12 months

I attached a draft proposal (proposal-v2.xlsx) and the usage summary (q3-usage-summary.csv) for quick context. High-level asks from ScaleGrid: predictable per-token unit price, ability to draw on the converted voucher pool without penalty, and an option to co-term with our annual price cadence.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can procurement confirm any internal constraints on voucher conversions (legal / tax / accounting limitations)?
2) If conversion is allowed, would ScaleGrid accept a blended-per-unit anchoring (example math in the attachment) plus a 12% uplift discount for the first 6 months to ease the transition?

Proposed timeline: internal pricing recommendation by Nov 2, customer-facing proposal by Nov 5, and final signature target Nov 20 to allow ops -> billing cutover before Dec.

Appreciate quick confirmation on conversion feasibility.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Jordan —

Thanks for the context and the files. We prefer conversions that don't force a complicated accounting reconciliation on our side. A couple of clarifying questions before I loop procurement:

- Is the proposed blended-per-unit anchoring you mentioned net of any one‑time conversion fee?
- If we co-term now, will the committed units reflect on the Dec invoice or be split across the remainder of the quarter?

I can get procurement engaged but they usually need a simple example (numbers) and the legal redline they should expect. Can you send a short example with final $/unit and the proposed conversion mechanics?

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@scalegrid.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: proposal to rebalance bundle and convert vouchers to top-up — pricing ask

Internal —

Forwarding ScaleGrid's clarifying questions. Need a compact set of options we can send Ava + procurement by EOD Nov 2. Keep the reply short; procurement prefers 1) examples with final $$ (per-embedding / per-token), 2) any one-time conversion fees, and 3) billing timing mechanics.

Suggested options (draft — please comment):

Option A — Voucher conversion -> Top-up + Co-term
- Convert remaining 200K voucher credits into 200K committed top-up units at an anchored blended rate of $0.0032/unit (anchored to historic usage).
- No one-time conversion fee if customer signs full 12‑month co-term.
- Billing: committed units appear on next monthly invoice (prorated for remainder of month), invoices reflect top-up draws until committed bucket is exhausted.

Option B — Partial conversion + credit buffer
- Convert 120K of vouchers to committed top-up units at $0.0034/unit; leave 80K as legacy vouchers that can be drawn down without invoicing until Q1 next year.
- One-time conversion processing fee: $750 (to cover KYC/billing adjustments).
- Billing: Converted units show as committed on co-term date; legacy vouchers spend separately and will be reported on usage report.

Option C — No conversion; blended discount on consumption
- Keep vouchers as legacy and apply a temporary blended discount of 12% on consumption pricing for the first 6 months, then 6% thereafter.
- No conversion fee.

Questions for pricing: can we offer an early-signing incentive (e.g., additional 3% discount) if ScaleGrid signs by Nov 20? Also flagging: legal will likely require a short amendment for voucher conversion; Irene, do we have a template?

Irene/Ben/Kimberly — recommend which of the above to send and any changes to the anchor rates.

—Jordan

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the clear options. My quick read: go with Option A as primary with Option B as fallback. Rationale: ScaleGrid's usage profile is already trending up; converting all vouchers to committed top-up yields cleaner unit economics and reduces billing complexity long term. Below are the example numbers you can drop into procurement:

- Starting point: historical blended cost = $0.0035/unit
- Option A (anchor $0.0032) gives ~8.6% unit improvement vs historical; with no one-time fee it’s easier for procurement to justify.
- Early-sign incentive: extra 3% off anchored rate if signed by Nov 20 -> $0.003104/unit for first 6 months.
- Example invoice timing: customer signs Nov 20; co-term effective Dec 1. For Nov: we prorate committed units for 10 days (Dec 1 start) and show a credit report for converted voucher balance. First full committed invoice posts Dec 1–30 cycle. Ops will need the signed amendment by Nov 22 to enable allocation.

Legal: Irene — please prepare the short amendment template (billing conversion clause + statement of remaining voucher balance) and loop in commercial counsel. Kimberly, please confirm billing-side processing time and whether we can waive the $750 fee for standard enterprise accounts; I'm comfortable waiving it for this book if we get the co-term.

Jordan — send this back to Ava with the anchor numbers and the early-sign incentive. Keep it short and include the amendment ETA.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
